pk/math.text: Rote count up to 20 in sequence
Count backwards from 10 to 0
Demonstrate one-to one correspondence when counting objects placed in a row (one to 15 and beyond)
Count out a specified number of objects up to 10
Understand that the last number represents how many objects are in a group
Understand that written numerals represent quantities of objects (up to 10)
Compare groups of objects and tell which is same or different, more, less, or fewer
Subitize (immediately recognize without counting) five or more objects
Identify written numerals from zero (0) up to 10
Match numerals with the correct number of objects, with assistance
Use addition and subtraction concepts while playing with sets of objects (0-10).
Independently change size of sets by combining or taking away
Understand that each successive number name refers to a quantity that is one larger
Match objects according to two or more attributes
Sort and place in a series objects according to more than attribute
Put up to 10 objects in order according to an attribute
Demonstrate knowledge that the same set can be sorted in different ways
Identify differences in the daily schedule or routine
Identify a pattern, and duplicate or extend
Create a more complex pattern that includes different attributes
Identify more complex ordinals, such as second, third, or next,
Visualize a spatial transformation
Describe the way in which objects fit together or verbally share plans with how to fit objects together
Move body in different ways independently or following directions in response to music or song
Identify and classify 2-D and 3-D shapes by their attributes
Visualize shapes by description and find them in the environment
Complete complex shape puzzles
Order objects in a series according to size
Use a variety of techniques with standard and non-standard tools to measure and compare objects
Compare objects by two or more attributes
Show a beginning awareness of the concept of time as a sequence of events
Use beginning skills of estimation in solving everyday measurement problems
Use trial and error to reach a solution to a problem
Gather data to answer questions to problems
Make a prediction based on data
Interpret a chart or graph to explain data findings

pk/language.text: Understand and follow multi-step directions
Recall the events described in a story
Respond to questions and extend answer to convey new, but related, thought
Attend to conversations and group discussions and respond on topic
Combine 5-8 words together into sentences
Engage in storytelling and pretend play, using oral language
Answer questions with detailed and more abstract words and ideas
Use mostly grammatically complex sentence structures
Have a vocabulary of over 1000 words
Ask specific questions to understand and solve problems.
Produce four to five word phrases using clear and understandable speech
Listen and respond on topic with individuals and during group conversations
Use language to communicate with others during familiar and unfamiliar social situations
Initiate conversations and stay on topic during at least 5 turn-taking exchanges
Demonstrate conversational rules of language
Identify characters and setting in a story
Use title, pictures, and prior knowledge to predict story content
Retell or act out a story in the correct sequence
Make connections between stories and reallife experiences
Answer questions about the characters and events in a story
Generalize idea to another situation
Identify whether or not two words start or end with the same sound
Produce rhyming words
Isolate and match the initial sounds in words with adult guidance
Segment words into syllables
Identify words as separate units in a sentence
Blend sounds with adult guidance
Recognize about half of the upper and lower case letters of the alphabet
Associate some letters of the alphabet with their specific sounds
Identify words that start with the same letter as their name
Visually discriminate letter shapes and formations
Sort letters and find words that contain specified letters
Select different kinds of literature
Show beginning understanding of word and sentence structure
Hold book correctly and read from beginning to end
Read some environmental print
Track words from left to right, top to bottom, page to page
Know that books have titles, authors, and illustrators
Write some letters of the alphabet, including name
Begin to use inventive spelling using a letter to represent a word

pk/science.text: Use the five senses to collect information
Try new approaches when results differ from what is expected
Form conclusions based on observable actions or results
Predict outcomes based on cause and effect, “If I…., then I….”
Describe differences between living and nonliving things
Describe how living things interact with the environment and its conditions to survive
Describe the functions of body parts
Describe the predictable patterns for life cycles of plants and animals
Experiment with cars, balls, and other objects to determine which is faster
Notice and explain changes in physical properties of objects as a result of outside influences
Describe characteristics of solids and liquids
Investigate the properties of light and sound
Compare and contrast the properties of natural materials, soil, and sand
Describe the properties and changes of water
Explore the characteristics of the sun and shadows, moon, clouds and stars
Explain how weather and its changes impact daily life
Describe the day and night cycle
Describe how changes to the environment occur
Discuss how actions positively and negatively impact the environment
Demonstrate conservation as part of daily routines
Describe the features of habitats that species need for life
Use or adapt appropriate tools and materials to create or solve problems
Use technology tools to seek out information or an answer to a problem
Explain the purposes of specific technology tools
Differentiate between real or pretend objects or situations
Discuss if information is realistic or could actually happen
Describe the specific uses for technology tools
Identify differences between packaging and what’s inside
Discuss the ways one can find out more information
Identify appropriate and inappropriate use of digital media
Collaborate with others to create a product or investigate information
Use technology terms such as mouse, keyboard, printer as part of daily conversation
Break down the steps of a problem or activity (Decomposition)
Extend and create design patterns (Pattern Recognition)
Attempt to solve a problem by working through the sequence of steps (Algorithms)
Assist teacher in sorting needed and unneeded information
Use unique materials to create a simple machine
Follow a visual plan to create a structure
Create detailed observational drawings that represent objects
Follow directional cues to accomplish a task

pk/social.text: Differentiate themselves by physical characteristics
Show increasingly accurate understanding of own strengths, preferences, limitations, and personal qualities
Connect adult’s actions to own accomplishments or actions
Make choices based on likes and dislikes (preferences)
Stand up for rights of others
Show confidence in ability by taking on new tasks
Show pride in completion of challenging tasks and activities
Invite peers to join play or activity
Describe accomplishments with detail
Associate basic emotions with words, expressions or gestures or actions
Communicate feelings or emotions in socially-acceptable ways
Seek reassurance or recognition from adults when attempting to resolve distress or challenging situation
Respond with empathy and compassion at others’ expression of emotion
Independently use self-regulation strategies to solve simple problems
Adapt behavior to accommodate situation or adult response
Independently solve simple problems
Transition to new activities independently when asked
Separate and easily accept explanation for parting with trusted adult
Cooperate with adult guidance to achieve adult approval
Initiate and engage with familiar adults to share mutual interests
Sustain relationships with other children for an extended period of time
Take the perspective of another child and respond in a manner that is supportive

Engage in prosocial behavior during play (cooperating, turn-taking, sharing)

Talk about relationships with other family members
Discuss how families differ and how they are the same
Differentiate groups they belong to
Follow routines and schedules

Show appreciation of own culture or customs

Describe occupations’ roles and purposes

Use the posted schedule to describe the day’s activities
Distinguish between events that happened in the past, present or future
Talk about an event that happened or will happen
Discuss past experiences or events in the correct sequence
Use time vocabulary with some accuracy
Use props and create characters as part of pretend play
Engage in elaborate and sustained imaginative play
Distinguish between real life and fantasy
Develop and sustain complex play themes and roles in cooperation with peers
Seek out specific children to engage in play experiences
Take another’s perspective
Articulate values and “rules” through play

Try things they are not sure they can do while avoiding dangerous risks
